name: How Big a Threat?
summary: How Big a Threat? is an Alliance quest given by Terenthis in Auberdine. Having witnessed furbolg madness taking root across Teldrassil, the night elf druid directs scouts to investigate local furbolg settlements in Darkshore to confirm whether the same dark taint has crossed the sea.

sections.title: Shadows Across the Sea
sections.body: The night elves of northern Kalimdor have long maintained cordial or peaceful relations with indigenous furbolg tribes. However, following the Third War, strange corruptions began unhinging furbolg minds in Teldrassil, resulting in violent kidnappings and feral attacks against their former allies. Stationed in Auberdine, the druid Terenthis fears that this sinister affliction is not isolated to the World Tree, but is actively spreading among the mainland tribes along the misty coasts of Darkshore.

sections.title: A Gathering Storm
sections.body: Reconnaissance of a furbolg encampment nestled near the ruins of Ameth'Aran confirms Terenthis's worst suspicions. The furbolgs there display erratic, hostile aggression, bearing the clear marks of the same corruption plaguing the north. Their close proximity to Auberdine elevates them from a peaceful wilderness neighbor to an urgent defensive hazard for the Alliance settlement.

aliases: who gives how big a threat
faq.answer: Terenthis is a night elf druid stationed in the coastal haven of Auberdine. Haunted by accounts of night elves assaulted and captured by maddened furbolgs across Teldrassil, he works to monitor and suppress emerging threats throughout Darkshore.

faq.q: Why are the furbolgs in Darkshore turning hostile?
faq.answer: Terenthis has seen hints of corruption in Darkshore and suspects the furbolgs may be affected, as some on Teldrassil were. He asks for their camps to be investigated because he has not yet established widespread signs.

faq.q: Where is the corrupt furbolg camp located?
faq.answer: The encampment lies inland in central Darkshore, situated just north of the ancient highborne ruins of Ameth'Aran and southeast of Auberdine.

faq.q: How does this relate to events on Teldrassil?
faq.answer: In Teldrassil, several corrupted furbolgs kidnapped and injured night elf sentinels and civilians. Terenthis references those recent rescues when seeking to verify if mainland Darkshore faces the exact same crisis.

faq.q: What happens after reporting back to Terenthis?
aliases: what follows how big a threat
faq.answer: Report any signs of corruption to Terenthis in Auberdine. His response to the findings is revealed when you return.

faq.q: Why are night elves so concerned about furbolg camps near Auberdine?
faq.answer: Auberdine serves as the principal Alliance port and supply lifeline on the mainland. Having deeply corrupted, hostile tribes nesting within striking distance leaves trade roads, scouting parties, and the town itself vulnerable to sudden assaults.

angles.text: For the kaldorei, watching ancient allies like the furbolgs succumb to irrational darkness so soon after the Third War is both a bitter tragedy and an immediate danger to sacred lands.
Furbolgs share deep bonds with nature and ancient wilderness spirits, making their sudden descent into corruption a grave concern for druids tasked with healing Kalimdor's balance.
As the Alliance's primary gateway to mainland northern Kalimdor, safeguarding Auberdine from wilderness threats is essential for regional security and logistics.
